title: فَ as the Connector of Immediate Sequence, كَاف التَّشْبِيه, and the Unmovable نُون النِّسْوَة
summary: The لَام التَّعْلِيل exercises are completed and the class reaches a point where it can parse وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ word by word. Lesson eighteen then brings three refinements: فَ as a حَرْف عَطْف conveying that one thing follows immediately on another, كَ as the particle of comparison, and the discovery that نُون النِّسْوَة is مَبْنِي — where أَنْ strips the نُون from other plural verbs, the feminine plural will not budge.
key_points: فَ is a حَرْف عَطْف, alongside وَ and ثُمَّ, but it conveys تَعْقِيب (taʿqīb) — that one thing comes directly after another, or follows as a result. وَ is simply and, ثُمَّ is then after an interval, and فَ is then at once.
This is why فَ often carries a sense of consequence: I opened the window to let in the air, فَدَخَلَ الذُّبَابُ — and so the fly came in. The purpose was the air; the fly was the result.
The teacher noted that even those who have memorised the Qur'ān sometimes confuse وَ and فَ in recitation, though each carries its own distinct meaning.

كَ is كَاف التَّشْبِيه (kāf al-tashbīh), a حَرْف الجَرّ meaning like or as, so the following noun takes a kasra: كَعَادَتِهِمْ, as is their habit. عَادَة means habit, as in Urdu, and كَالْعَادَةِ serves for as usual.

نُون النِّسْوَة (nūn al-niswah : the nūn of the women) is مَبْنِي — it never changes under any circumstance. So while تَذْهَبُونَ loses its نُون after أَنْ, تَذْهَبْنَ does not: تُرِدْنَ أَنْ تَأْخُذْنَ stays intact.
The first person makes no distinction of gender: أُرِيدُ and نُرِيدُ serve for male and female alike, singular and plural. Only the second and third persons have separate feminine forms.
أَنْ followed by لَا is written together as أَلَّا — أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ is really أَنْ plus لَا, and وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا likewise.
عِنْدَ is a ظَرْف indicating place or time, used for being at someone's place: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ الْجَارَةِ, I was at the neighbour's — hence رُجُوعُكِ مِنْ عِنْدِ الْجَارَةِ rather than مِنَ الْجَارَةِ.
عِيَادَة is specifically visiting someone who is ill, as in Urdu; general visiting is زَارَ، يَزُورُ with its مَصْدَر زِيَارَة.
اِشْتَرَى، يَشْتَرِي (to buy) belongs to the added verb patterns still to be covered, beyond the فَعَّلَ and أَفْعَلَ already introduced.
A word ending in a long alif such as مُسْتَشْفَى cannot show its kasra; the ending is there grammatically but invisible.
حَيَّا بِنَا means come, let us go — heard in the adhān as حَيَّ.

Vocabulary: شَرِيف (noble), بَرْقِيَّة (telegram), هَوَاء (air, as in Urdu), ذُبَاب (a fly), مَتْحَف (museum), عُلْبَة (box), لِبَاس with its plural مَلَابِس (clothing), مَسْطَرَة with مَسَاطِر (rulers), جَارَة (a female neighbour), كَوَى، يَكْوِي (to iron) with its مِكْوَاة, and سَمَحَ (to permit).
questions: [00:04:00] Q: Is هَوَاء the word for as a result? — A: No, هَوَاء means air or wind, as in Urdu. The sense of as a result comes from the فَ.
[00:05:00] Q: How does فَ differ from وَ and ثُمَّ? — A: All three connect, but وَ is simply and, ثُمَّ is then after some time, and فَ means immediately after, often with the sense of consequently.
[00:25:00] Q: Which word does كَ put in the kasra, and what does it add? — A: It is a حَرْف الجَرّ, so the noun after it takes a kasra, and it conveys comparison — the full name is كَاف التَّشْبِيه.
[00:26:01] Q: Is كَعَادَتِهِمْ a single word meaning as usual? — A: The underlying word is عَادَة, habit; كَعَادَتِهِمْ means as is their habit, and the phrase does the work of as usual.
[00:28:00] Q: Is عِيَادَة the general word for visiting? — A: No — عِيَادَة is visiting a sick person specifically. General visiting is زَارَ، يَزُورُ، زِيَارَة, the word used for going for ziyārah.

[00:29:00] Q: Why didn't the نُون drop here after أَنْ, as the rule said? — A: Because this is نُون النِّسْوَة, which is مَبْنِي and never changes. Once the subject is a group of women, nothing alters the form.
[00:31:00] Q: Shouldn't it be نُرِيدْنَ for a group of females? — A: No. The first person has one form regardless of gender or number, so both men and women say نُرِيدُ.
[00:33:00] Q: Why is there no visible kasra on مُسْتَشْفَى? — A: Because of the long alif at its end; the ending is grammatically there but cannot be shown.
[00:36:00] Q: Have we seen أَنْ followed by لَا before? — A: Yes — أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ and وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا are both this combination, written joined.

quiz.q: What meaning does فَ add that وَ does not?
options: تَعْقِيب — that one thing follows immediately, often as a result
quiz.a: وَ is simply and; فَ signals immediate sequence or consequence, as in فَدَخَلَ الذُّبَابُ.

quiz.q: How does ثُمَّ differ from فَ?
options: ثُمَّ means and; فَ means then
ثُمَّ means then after an interval; فَ means then at once
quiz.a: Both can be rendered then, but only ثُمَّ allows for a gap in time.

quiz.q: What is the full name of the كَ of comparison, and what does it do grammatically?
options: كَاف التَّشْبِيه — a حَرْف الجَرّ, so the next word takes a kasra
كَاف التَّعْلِيل — it gives a reason
كَاف الِاسْتِفْهَام — it asks a question
quiz.a: تَشْبِيه is comparison, and like any حَرْف الجَرّ it puts the following noun in the genitive.
The same word as Urdu ʿādat, so كَعَادَتِهِمْ is as is their habit.

quiz.q: Why does the نُون not drop in تُرِدْنَ أَنْ تَأْخُذْنَ?
options: Because أَنْ only affects masculine verbs
Because نُون النِّسْوَة is مَبْنِي and never changes
Because the verb is past tense
quiz.a: Unlike the نُون of تَذْهَبُونَ, the feminine plural nūn is fixed and immune to أَنْ.
It does not alter whatever precedes it — the property of نُون النِّسْوَة.

quiz.q: Which form do women use for we want?
quiz.a: The first person has one form for both genders, so نُرِيدُ serves everyone.

quiz.q: What two words make up أَلَّا?
quiz.a: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ shows the pair, written joined as أَلَّا elsewhere.

quiz.q: Which word is used for visiting someone who is ill?
quiz.a: عِيَادَة is specific to the sick; زِيَارَة is visiting in general.

quiz.q: Why can مُسْتَشْفَى not show a kasra?
options: Because of the long alif at the end, which prevents the vowel appearing
quiz.a: The ending is grammatically present but cannot be written on the final alif.

quran_examples.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-mā khalaqtu al-jinna wa-l-insa illā li-yaʿbudūn
quran_examples.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
quran_examples.note: The teacher parsed this fully with the class as a mark of how far they had come: مَا negating the مَاضِي, الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ as مَفْعُول بِهِ with the fatḥa, إِلَّا meaning except, and لِيَعْبُدُونِ carrying لَام التَّعْلِيل.

quran_examples.arabic: فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُ وَابِلٌ فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدًا
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-mathaluhu ka-mathali ṣafwānin ʿalayhi turābun fa-aṣābahu wābilun fa-tarakahu ṣaldā
quran_examples.translation: His likeness is that of a smooth stone upon which is dust, and a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for كَاف التَّشْبِيه — كَمَثَلِ with its kasra — and the āyah also shows فَ three times carrying exactly the sequence-and-consequence sense taught here.

quran_examples.arabic: لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ
quran_examples.transliteration: laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun, wa-huwa al-samīʿu al-baṣīr
quran_examples.translation: There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
quran_examples.note: A second instance of كَاف التَّشْبِيه, raised in class, and it opens with لَيْسَ from the earlier lessons.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-qaḍā rabbuka allā taʿbudū illā iyyāh
quran_examples.translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example of أَنْ joined to لَا as أَلَّا — and تَعْبُدُوا has lost its نُون after أَنْ, exactly the rule being drilled.

quran_examples.arabic: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا
quran_examples.transliteration: yurīdūna an yakhrujū mina al-nāri wa-mā hum bi-khārijīna minhā
quran_examples.translation: They will wish to come out of the Fire, but they will never come out of it.
quran_examples.note: The masculine plural losing its نُون after أَنْ — يَخْرُجُونَ becoming يَخْرُجُوا — set against the feminine plural, which keeps its نُون.
